headline: OpenAI shuts down Atlas browser to integrate AI browsing into ChatGPT
summary: The AI-powered browser launched in October is being discontinued, with its features moving to ChatGPT's desktop app and a new Chrome extension.
details: OpenAI is sunsetting Atlas, its AI-powered browser, just months after its October launch. The company is shifting its focus to integrating AI browsing capabilities directly into existing platforms.
Instead of a standalone browser, OpenAI is now distributing Atlas's agentic browsing features across ChatGPT's desktop application and a new Google Chrome extension.

This move follows a broader industry trend where companies like Perplexity and Google have experimented with AI-enhanced browsing. OpenAI appears to have concluded that the browser itself is a feature, not a primary destination for users.

The new ChatGPT extension for Chrome will allow users to interact with webpages, ask questions, and summarize content directly from their browser, aiming to compete with features like Google's Gemini Side Panel.

Additionally, the ChatGPT desktop app is receiving an upgrade with a more robust browser, enabling users to browse, log into accounts, and download files without leaving the application. This includes a remote cloud browser for agent tasks.
These updates aim to transform ChatGPT into a continuous workspace that seamlessly integrates across Chrome, the desktop app, and AI agents, offering a more unified user experience.

headline: Elon Musk Praises Anthropic's AI Models
summary: Elon Musk praises Anthropic's AI models, promises not to cut them off
details: Elon Musk has praised Anthropic's AI models, specifically Mythos/Fable, and promised not to cut them off from SpaceX's infrastructure. This comes after concerns were raised about Musk potentially shutting down Anthropic's access to SpaceX's servers.
Anthropic has signed a deal with SpaceX to use 300 megawatts of compute from xAI's Colossus 1 data center, worth $40 billion in revenue for SpaceX's xAI unit. The deal runs through May 2029.
Musk cited his company's history of not initiating patent lawsuits against those who want to use its technology, and opening its Supercharger network and charging port design to competitors.
caption:
Elon Musk praises Anthropic's AI models. Will he keep his promise?

Elon Musk has praised Anthropic's AI models, specifically Mythos/Fable, and promised not to cut them off from SpaceX's infrastructure. This comes after concerns were raised about Musk potentially shutting down Anthropic's access to SpaceX's servers.

Anthropic has signed a deal with SpaceX to use 300 megawatts of compute from xAI's Colossus 1 data center, worth $40 billion in revenue for SpaceX's xAI unit. The deal runs through May 2029.

Musk cited his company's history of not initiating patent lawsuits against those who want to use its technology, and opening its Supercharger network and charging port design to competitors.
